is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles funestus and Anopheles gambiae (Page 1, Title).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study genotypes Vgsc L1014F, L1014S, and Ace-1 G119S in An. gambiae, and GSTe2 L119F, Rdl A296S, and Cyp6p9a in An. funestus (Page 2, Results; Page 7, Genotyping section).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Genotype counts and allele frequencies are provided for both species. For An. gambiae (n=39): L1014F (36 RR, 2 RS, 1 SS), L1014S (1 RS, 38 SS), and G119S (6 RR, 1 RS, 32 SS). For An. funestus (n=50): L119F-GSTe2 (4 RR, 40 RS, 6 SS), A296S-RDL (50 RR), and Cyp6p9a (50 SS) (Pages 9-10).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from houses in Elende, Cameroon, in April 2019 (Page 4, Methods).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study reporting original collection and molecular analysis data.

sub_country_location.evidence: Data is tied to Elende (3°41’57.27’’N, 11°33’28.46’’E), a locality near Yaoundé, Cameroon (Page 4, Methods).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected in April 2019 (Page 4, Methods).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study is a primary research article for a specific locality; while the authors are affiliated with major research centers (CRID, LSTM), there is no indication that this specific dataset is a subset of a larger published work.

supplement.evidence: All necessary genotype counts and frequencies are provided in the main text and Figure 4.

assessment.summary: This study characterized malaria vectors in Elende, a peri-urban forested locality near Yaoundé, Cameroon, in April 2019. Both Anopheles funestus and Anopheles gambiae exhibited high resistance to pyrethroids and DDT. Molecular analysis of field-collected F0 mosquitoes revealed high frequencies of resistance markers: in An. gambiae, Vgsc L995F was nearly fixed (95% allele frequency) and Ace-1 G280S was present at 17% allele frequency; in An. funestus, GSTe2 L119F was found at 48% allele frequency and Rdl A296S was fixed (100% RR). Vgsc L995S was rare in An. gambiae (1.3%), and the Cyp6p9a resistant allele was absent in An. funestus.
